subject: Harbor Bank — recovery commitments Q&A and runbook excerpt
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@harborbank.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@harborbank.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Initial DR clarifications — RTO/RPO specifics and multi-region acceptance

Hannah,

Thanks again for the RFP submission. We are reviewing the disaster recovery sections and have a few clarifying questions before we lock acceptance criteria with our Ops and Procurement teams:

1) For the critical inference path (model serving + KV cache), can you confirm the attainable RTO and RPO for single-region failure vs. full AZ outage in the same region? Please give numeric RTO (minutes) and RPO (seconds/minutes) and note any dependency on model size (e.g., >30B).

2) How does automated failover behave when there is in-flight state (KV cache warm) — do you support transparent KV rehydration, or do clients need to re-prime?

3) For multi-region failover, is the switchover synchronous or eventual with DNS TTL-based cutover? What is your recommended TTL and the expected additional reconvergence time?

4) We will need a short excerpt of the runbook showing the failover steps and who gets paged. Can you attach a redacted extract?

Appreciate concise answers — we want to include them in the procurement appendix. If helpful, we can schedule a 30-minute technical Q&A later this week.

Best,
Samir Patel
Sr. SRE, Harbor Bank

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@harborbank.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@harborbank.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 13:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial DR clarifications — RTO/RPO specifics and multi-region acceptance

Samir — thanks for the clear list. I answered inline and attached a short runbook extract + appendix for your procurement team. High level answers first, then details below.

High level
- Single-region (AZ) outage: RTO = 3–7 minutes typical (5 minutes SLA target for Critical tier); RPO = near-zero for persisted objects; for large models (>30B) cold-start extension up to 15 minutes unless warm replicas are provisioned.
- Full-region outage: RTO = 10–30 minutes depending on capacity warm-standby and data egress policies; RPO = up to 5 minutes for session-level state unless KV cache is externally checkpointed.
- KV cache behavior: transparent rehydration supported for customer-managed warm caches; ephemeral session caches should be re-primed by client — we provide automated delta-sync tooling to reduce re-prime windows to seconds.
- Multi-region cutover: our default is DNS-backed cutover with active-active routing for stateless inference and stateful routing using a control-plane switch (we recommend TTL=30s for minimal propagation delay). Expected reconvergence after DNS change: typically 1–3 minutes for most CDN/ISP mixes; allow up to 10 minutes for worst-case networks.

Detailed answers (by question)
1) RTO / RPO numeric table (summary):
- Critical inference path (small/medium models <30B): AZ outage RTO = 3–5 min; RPO < 30s. Region outage RTO = 10–15 min; RPO < 2 min.
- Large models (>30B): AZ outage RTO = 5–10 min (due to weight loading); region outage RTO = 15–30 min if model needs to be re-provisioned; RPO = 1–5 min depending on checkpoint cadence.

2) KV cache resiliency:
- We persist checkpointed KV snapshots to customer-configured object storage every N minutes (configurable). If snapshots exist, rehydration is automated; otherwise we fall back to re-prime.
- For Dedicated customers we offer synchronous replication options for critical keys.

3) Multi-region failover mechanics:
- Stateless routes: active-active with geo-routing control-plane; cutover is effectively immediate once routing rules change.
- Stateful sessions: control-plane issues a switchover and updates session ownership; this is a control-plane switch (not pure DNS) for sub-5-minute handoffs when warm replicas exist.
- DNS recommendation: 30s TTL plus health-check-driven routing.

4) Runbook extract: attached (Harbor_RFP_DR_Appendix_v1.pdf) + CSV extract of the failover sequence.

Attachments:
- Harbor_RFP_DR_Appendix_v1.pdf (redacted runbook excerpt, RTO/RPO table, escalation matrix)
- failover-sequence-extract.csv (ordered steps for automated switchover)

Next steps:
- If those numbers meet your ops acceptance envelope, happy to lock them into the procurement appendix and provide an annotated timeline for a runbook rehearsal.
- I can join a call Thursday or Friday (PST).

Regards,
Hannah Schmitt
Principal SRE Partner, Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0143

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@harborbank.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@harborbank.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial DR clarifications — RTO/RPO specifics and multi-region acceptance

Samir, Hannah — looping in a few implementation notes from the infra side. A couple of clarifications below (quoting Hannah where helpful):

> "Large models (>30B): AZ outage RTO = 5–10 min (due to weight loading)"
- To be explicit: if you expect sub-5 minute RTO for large models, we need reserved warm capacity (dedicated pool) in target regions and pre-pulled artifacts. That is an additional procurement line-item; we can provide a capacity worksheet if helpful.

> "We persist checkpointed KV snapshots to customer-configured object storage every N minutes"
- Note: snapshot frequency is configurable per workload. Default is 5 minutes. For RPO targets under 1 minute we recommend streaming checkpoints to your object store (we can support that via our connector).

Operational asks for your runbook acceptance: 
- Please confirm the list of on-call roles to be notified on failover: Harbor Ops Lead, Harbor Network, Redwood On-call (SRE), Redwood CS. We included a redacted escalation matrix in the PDF.
- We suggest a staged rehearsal: 1) tabletop, 2) partial failover (non-critical region), 3) full cutover rehearsal. Each stage has pass/fail criteria in the appendix.

If you want I can prepare the capacity worksheet and include cost delta for reserved warm pools for the large-model SLA. Shall I send that to procurement?

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Infra Reliability — Redwood Inference

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@harborbank.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial DR clarifications — RTO/RPO specifics and multi-region acceptance

Samir — thanks for the questions and team for the quick answers. Procurement asked me to confirm a couple of contractual items before we finalize language in the SOW:

1) SLA language: we will include a Critical-tier RTO target of 5 minutes (AZ) and a region failover target of 15 minutes in the SOW, with credits triggered on missed targets. We will mark large-model coverage as an opt-in addendum tied to reserved warm capacity.

2) Evidence: procurement requires one recorded rehearsal (non-production) and the annotated runbook before go-live. We can schedule the rehearsal window within 30 days of contract signature.

3) Acceptance criteria: please confirm Harbor's on-call list (Karthik noted roles above). Once we have that we will prepare the final appendix for signature and attach the rehearsal test plan.

I attached a short link to the draft appendix in our shared workspace and timeline for the rehearsal.

Attachments / Links:
- Draft Appendix (Harbor_RFP_DR_Appendix_v1.pdf) — redacted
- Rehearsal timeline: https://app.redwood.ai/shared/Harbor-RFP-2026/rehearsal-plan

If that aligns I will update the SOW language and circulate for signature.

Regards,
Grace O'Connor
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
